newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Narrower loss sparks jump in troubled Toco.
newsitem.headline: Narrower loss sparks jump in troubled Toco.

text.p: South African industrial firm Toco Holdings surged 25 percent on Monday, fuelled by the company narrowing its year loss substantially, dealers said.
By 0920 GMT the share had gained nine cents to 45 cents with 1.6 million shares changing hands.
"It's starting to look like they're sorting out their problems and there's some promise here," one dealer said.
Toco has suffered for most of the year, sliding at the hands of a series of profit warnings.
On June 17 it fell to 33 cents, its lowest ever. As recently as last Novemeber Toco was trading at 380 cents.

Toco issued a profit warning in April saying that full year attributable earnings had not been as favourable as it had anticipated. Then on May 29 the firm said it had received an urgent provisional winding-up order for one of its subsidiaries, Inn Group Holdings (Pty) Ltd.
Dealers said the stock was starting to show signs of recovery and the slimmer loss was sparking interest.
Toco earlier on Monday posted a year headline loss of 13 cents per share compared to a loss of 115 cents per share for the year ended March 31.

The company also said a radical restructuring now meant most of the group's trading units were operating satisfactorily with strong prospects of recording substantial earnings increases in the short to medium-term.
Toco said it was confident it could return to profitability by the end of the next financial year.
"A lot of its troubles seem to be coming to an end and its pulling itself right after a very bad couple of years," a dealer said.
